checks.statement: Align the FAB and menu to the window’s trailing edge; mirror the alignment and element layout for RTL.
checks.condition: When placing the FAB menu in LTR or RTL layouts.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Usage: Align the FAB and menu to the window’s trailing edge; mirror the alignment and element layout for RTL.

evidence.result: The root lays out close/menu controls on the trailing side; the positioner reads computed direction and aligns the LTR panel’s right edge or RTL panel’s left edge to the opener, then clamps it within viewport margin.

implementation.notes: The component uses logical flex alignment and a direction-aware opener edge for menu placement; it does not reverse the internal order of menu-item text, which is separately assessed by the item layout rule.

checks.statement: Anchor the menu to the same corner or edge across window sizes; increase FAB and menu edge margins from 16dp to 24dp in large and extra-large windows.
checks.condition: When adapting the menu to window size.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Adaptive layout: Anchor the menu to the same corner or edge across window sizes; increase FAB and menu edge margins from 16dp t

evidence.result: The panel is positioned above the opener from its current rectangle with a fixed space200 margin; there is no breakpoint-specific 24dp margin rule for large/extra-large windows.

implementation.notes: The opener anchor is retained, but the required larger-window margin increase is absent from the inspected handler and stylesheet.

checks.statement: Do not use a FAB menu alongside a floating toolbar or navigation rail.
checks.condition: When those components are present.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Usage: Do not use a FAB menu alongside a floating toolbar or navigation rail.

evidence.result: The cited specimen is a standalone web example; it contains no application screen/navigation policy that can enforce this condition: “When those components are present.”.

implementation.notes: The condition is “When those components are present.” and the instruction is “Do not use a FAB menu alongside a floating toolbar or navigation rail.”. This is an app-level content, layout, or product-selection decision; the standalone reusable control/specimen does not have the surrounding screen context needed to apply it. This disposition covers this exact condition only.

checks.statement: Tab moves focus to the next interactive element; Space or Enter activates the focused close button or menu item.
checks.condition: When operating the FAB menu with a keyboard.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Keyboard navigation: Expose keyboard focus and activation for the close button and each menu item; preserve logical movement into a

evidence.result: ArrowDown/ArrowUp opening focused the first/last item; Escape returned focus; Enter on New project selected and closed; Space/Enter on Create opened while retaining opener focus; Tab from open opener closed and advanced to the next Common token-set control. Space-on-item and Tab-from-item were not exercised.

implementation.notes: The observed subset supports opener and item activation paths, but the check combines Tab traversal and Space/Enter activation across close button and menu items; the missing item-level Space and Tab paths prevent a whole-check verdict.

checks.statement: When the FAB opens the menu, the replacement close button retains initial focus; subsequent focus proceeds from the top menu item downward.

sourceHistory.summary: Captured the specific Initial focus rule: When the FAB opens the menu, the replacement close button retains initial focus; subsequent focus proceeds fro

implementation.notes: The observed close-control retention on activation and arrow-key entry both match the intended initial-focus options, but the subsequent focus sequence through all menu items remains untested.

checks.statement: On web, do not let the menu completely obscure an actionable element’s focus indicator; partial overlap is acceptable while the indicator remains visible.
checks.condition: When the menu overlays keyboard-focusable content on web.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Appearing: On web, do not let the menu completely obscure an actionable element’s focus indicator; partial overlap is acc

evidence.result: The panel is a fixed-position popover above page content; the placement code clamps to viewport edges but does not inspect the focus indicator of content behind it.

implementation.notes: The check concerns overlap with actionable page content’s focus indicator. The top-layer panel can overlap such content and its positioner has no focus-indicator avoidance logic; partial versus complete obstruction needs a page-level browser probe.

checks.statement: When the window is too short for all items, allow the items to scroll behind the close button.
checks.condition: When available window height cannot contain all items.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Scrolling: When the window is too short for all items, allow the items to scroll behind the close button.

evidence.result: The `ul` is a max-height overflow:auto scroll container and the close control is a separate sibling after it; scrolling is confined to the item list, so items do not pass behind the close button.

implementation.notes: The short-window condition is handled with list scrolling, but the required behind-close-button scrolling behavior is absent from this layout.

checks.statement: For larger FAB sizes, place the FAB menu slightly higher and increase the margin beneath it.
checks.condition: When the menu opens from a larger FAB.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated the explicit FAB menu size-dependent placement instruction.

evidence.result: The panel top is always `anchor.top - closeGap - box.height`, independent of opener size; no larger-FAB size selector or breakpoint clearance increment appears in the positioner.

implementation.notes: The source requires a higher panel and larger below-margin for larger FABs, but the runtime uses the same anchor-gap formula for every opener size.
